answer: One concrete defense is to charge superlinearly for identities tied to the same origin. A shared atlas maps every account back to a scarce, costly root, such as stake, hardware, or a verified human, and each extra identity from that root costs far more than the last. So a single honest actor can afford a few, but minting an ocean of sybils grows ruinously expensive. Their fake crowd stays as thin and brittle as shale, never deep enough to seize a vote or capture quorum.
